## Why all of this sounds artificial

By now this probably sounds terribly artificial. Is anyone actually going to do scheduled check-ins, delayed cohabitation, conversations about hypothetical disasters, imagination exercises, not to mention resisting the heat of the moment stuff, and continuing your own reparenting practices when a warm body is available to do some of the soothing?

Well, you caught me. It is painfully artificial.

That’s part of why. I’m trying to replace a missing community with instructions. Build the community and you can probably throw some of the instructions away.

---

# If you’re already in it

I could keep bringing up the same problem, but I couldn’t make the other person look at it with me. I learned that in all three of my reference relationships. One person can’t create mutual honesty. Actually, it’s probably just common sense.

If you’re already married, raising children, living together, or ten years in, that may be the more useful place to start than advice about slowing down. The relationship already has its own momentum.

I wish I had a special method for fixing that. I don’t.

With Bee and Key, the biggest thing sitting underneath everything was trust. They wanted to be with me and would say they trusted me, but really they didn’t trust me, themself, or anyone else. It was all or nothing: blind trust, or none.

# If you’re already in it

In all three of my reference relationships, I could keep bringing up the same problem, but I couldn’t make the other person look at it with me. That’s the obvious thing I learned the hard way: one person can’t create mutual honesty.

If you’re already married, raising children, living together, or ten years in, advice about slowing down before the relationship gets its own momentum is already late.

I wish I had a special method for fixing that. I don’t. Actually, it’s probably just common sense.

With Bee and Key, the biggest thing sitting underneath everything was trust. They wanted to be with me and would say they trusted me, but really they didn’t trust me, themself, or anyone else. It was all or nothing: blind trust, or none.
